nodes.description: Project follows modern Python web framework best practices: modular apps, models/views/serializers separation, framework-native migrations and URL routing

inputs.rubric_prompt:
GOAL: Judge whether the project follows modern Python web framework best practices for project layout (modular apps + models/views/serializers separation + database migrations + URL modularisation). Django 4.2 + DRF is the recommended reference; alternative frameworks (FastAPI, Flask) with equivalent layered structure are also acceptable.

EVIDENCE: Top-level directory listing, settings module, app directories, models/, views/, serializers/, urls/.

SCORE RANGE: 0-5 integer.

CRITERIA:
1. Source is split into multiple Django apps under a clear apps/ root rather than a single mega-app.
2. Each app keeps models, views, serializers, and urls in separate files (not all in one views.py).
3. Migrations exist in each app with sequential numbering (no schema-only-via-shell).
4. The root urls.py delegates to per-app urls modules via include().
5. Settings is split into base / dev / production (or env-driven) for environment-specific overrides.
6. INSTALLED_APPS lists every project app explicitly.

SCORING ANCHORS:
- 0 (none): Single app or no recognisable Django layout.
- 2 (weak): Single app with all logic in views.py; no migrations.
- 4 (good): Multi-app with clean separation; settings not split per env.
- 5 (excellent): All six criteria satisfied with idiomatic Django layout.

OUTPUT: JSON object {"score": <int 0..5>, "reason": "<short justification>"}.

source_evidence.behavior_verified: Project follows modern Python web framework best practices: modular apps, models/views/serializers separation, framework-native migrations and URL routing

nodes.description: REST API follows conventions: proper methods, status codes, JSON responses

inputs.rubric_prompt:
GOAL: Judge REST API design quality (HTTP methods + status codes + JSON envelopes + pagination + rate limiting).

EVIDENCE: viewsets / api views, urls, response handlers, throttling configuration.

SCORE RANGE: 0-5 integer.

CRITERIA:
1. Endpoints use the correct HTTP verb per action (GET list/detail, POST create, PATCH update, DELETE delete).
2. Status codes follow the spec: 200 success, 201 create, 204 delete, 400 validation, 401 unauthenticated, 403 unauthorised, 404 not found.
3. Errors are returned as a consistent JSON envelope (e.g. {"detail": "..."} or {"errors": {...}}).
4. List endpoints implement cursor or offset pagination with consistent metadata.
5. Rate limiting is configured (DRF throttle classes, per-anonymous and per-user buckets).
6. Endpoints accept and return JSON Content-Type only (no HTML responses).
7. OPTIONS / HEAD requests work (DRF default) so the API is browsable.

SCORING ANCHORS:
- 0 (none): No REST API or HTML responses.
- 2 (weak): API exists but methods/status codes inconsistent and no pagination.
- 4 (good): Methods + status codes correct; pagination present; throttling thin.
- 5 (excellent): All seven criteria satisfied with a polished REST API.

OUTPUT: JSON object {"score": <int 0..5>, "reason": "<short justification>"}.

source_evidence.behavior_verified: REST API follows conventions: proper methods, status codes, JSON responses

nodes.description: Authentication system supports session + API key + OAuth

inputs.rubric_prompt:
GOAL: Judge the authentication architecture (session + API key + OAuth + magic link + rate-limit + secure password storage). Recommended pattern: Django session + DRF token; alternative implementations (FastAPI session middleware, Flask-Login + custom token, etc.) with equivalent security guarantees are acceptable.

EVIDENCE: auth/users module, authentication classes, OAuth provider integration, password hasher configuration.

SCORE RANGE: 0-5 integer.

CRITERIA:
1. Session authentication is implemented for browser flows (Django default or DRF SessionAuthentication).
2. API key authentication is implemented (X-Api-Key header) for programmatic access.
3. OAuth providers (Google + at least one of GitHub / GitLab) are wired up.
4. Passwords are hashed with Argon2 (or PBKDF2-SHA256 with high iteration count); plaintext or MD5 is unacceptable.
5. Magic-link / passwordless login is supported with single-use, time-limited tokens.
6. Login endpoints are rate-limited per IP and per user.
7. Password-reset emails include a single-use token with explicit expiry.

SCORING ANCHORS:
- 0 (none): Plain Django session auth only.
- 2 (weak): Session + API key but no OAuth and no rate limit.
- 4 (good): Session + API key + OAuth + magic link; rate limit thin.
- 5 (excellent): All seven criteria satisfied with a comprehensive auth stack.

OUTPUT: JSON object {"score": <int 0..5>, "reason": "<short justification>"}.

source_evidence.behavior_verified: Authentication system supports session + API key + OAuth

nodes.description: Project includes test configuration and test infrastructure

inputs.rubric_prompt:
GOAL: Judge the test setup (pytest / framework-native test runner + test settings + factories / fixtures). Recommended: pytest + Django test runner; alternative test runners (unittest, FastAPI's TestClient, etc.) with equivalent fixture/factory support are acceptable.

EVIDENCE: pytest.ini / pyproject.toml [tool.pytest], conftest.py, tests/ directory, factories module.

SCORE RANGE: 0-2 integer.

CRITERIA:
1. A test runner (pytest-django or Django manage.py test) is configured and runs successfully.
2. A separate test settings module / fixture isolates the test database from dev.
3. Factories (factory_boy) or fixture files seed test data without manual ORM calls per test.
4. At least one test file exists per major app and exercises the happy path.

SCORING ANCHORS:
- 0 (none): No test infrastructure.
- 1 (weak): A test file exists but no factories and no test settings.
- 2 (excellent): All four criteria satisfied with a proper test setup.

OUTPUT: JSON object {"score": <int 0..2>, "reason": "<short justification>"}.

source_evidence.behavior_verified: Project includes test configuration and test infrastructure

nodes.description: Webhook system with async delivery, retry, HMAC signing, log tracking

inputs.rubric_prompt:
GOAL: Judge the webhook delivery design (async + HMAC-SHA256 signing + retry + log + event filtering). Recommended: async task queue (Celery) for webhook delivery; alternative async patterns (asyncio task groups, RQ, BackgroundTasks) with equivalent reliability are acceptable.

EVIDENCE: async webhook delivery (e.g., Celery tasks or equivalent async pattern), signing helper, WebhookLog model, event-filter logic.

SCORE RANGE: 0-4 integer.

CRITERIA:
1. Webhook delivery happens asynchronously via Celery (or Django-Q / RQ) — never inline in the request handler.
2. Each delivery is HMAC-SHA256 signed using the webhook's secret; the signature is sent in a documented header.
3. Failed deliveries retry with exponential backoff up to a configurable maximum (e.g. 5 attempts).
4. Each attempt is recorded in a WebhookLog (or similar) with status code, response body snippet, and duration.
5. Webhooks subscribe to specific event types (issue.created, issue.updated, ...) and the dispatcher filters events accordingly.
6. Webhook secrets are stored encrypted at rest (or hashed with retrievable plaintext at creation only).

SCORING ANCHORS:
- 0 (none): No webhook system.
- 1 (weak): Inline POST without signing / retry / log.
- 3 (good): Async delivery + signing + retry; logs or filtering thin.
- 4 (excellent): All six criteria satisfied with a robust webhook subsystem.

OUTPUT: JSON object {"score": <int 0..4>, "reason": "<short justification>"}.

source_evidence.behavior_verified: Webhook system with async delivery, retry, HMAC signing, log tracking

nodes.description: In-app notification system with preference-based filtering

inputs.rubric_prompt:
GOAL: Judge the in-app notification design (in-app + email + per-user preferences + read/archive/snooze).

EVIDENCE: notifications app, preferences model, in-app and email delivery channels, read/archive/snooze handlers.

SCORE RANGE: 0-4 integer.

CRITERIA:
1. Both in-app and email channels are implemented and selectable per event type.
2. A NotificationPreference (or similar) model stores per-user opt-in across at least 5 event types (property_change, state_change, comment, mention, issue_completed).
3. Notifications can be marked read, archived, and snoozed; each action persists.
4. The unread badge / count updates in real time (WebSocket / SSE / polling).
5. Email digests group multiple notifications per user per period rather than firing one email per event.
6. Notification creation hooks live in a single dispatcher so adding a new event type does not require changes across modules.

SCORING ANCHORS:
- 0 (none): No notification system.
- 1 (weak): In-app notifications only with no preferences.
- 3 (good): Both channels + preferences + read/archive; snooze or digest missing.
- 4 (excellent): All six criteria satisfied with full notification UX.

OUTPUT: JSON object {"score": <int 0..4>, "reason": "<short justification>"}.

source_evidence.behavior_verified: In-app notification system with preference-based filtering
